name: Richard Spencer
role: American white nationalist activist, publisher, and former National Policy Institute president
summary: Spencer advocated a pan-European white ethnostate and argued that a governing elite should have distinct political rights. He has supported government-backed health coverage and, in later writing, Western security guarantees for Ukraine.

abortion-legal.rationale: Asked whether he supported abortion, Spencer said he generally supported legal abortion rights in the United States.

civilizational-union.rationale: Spencer’s stated goal was a common political home for European peoples across existing national boundaries.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Spencer explicitly envisioned the imperial center supporting dependent peoples indefinitely and expected resources to flow to them.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Spencer criticized consumerism as a motivating force in contemporary culture and argued that acquisitiveness lay behind what he called the commercialized language of liberation.

culture-before-state.rationale: Spencer treated the cultivation of a shared racial consciousness as a prerequisite for creating his proposed homeland.

democracy-best.rationale: Spencer preferred an authoritarian arrangement with a protective elite and described recurring mass elections as a waste of resources.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Spencer explicitly distinguished governing for the people from parliamentary procedure and said even an oligarchy or dictatorship could express democracy in his sense.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Spencer proposed that his envisioned white homeland grant a right of return to every white person regardless of birthplace.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Spencer explicitly opposed interracial marriage and having children across racial lines, which he claimed would dissolve existing racial identities.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Spencer argued that bringing different racial and cultural groups together erodes trust and creates conflict.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Spencer described Ukraine’s integration into NATO as a means of preserving its independence and later rejected a permanent veto on NATO enlargement. He acknowledged having promoted Russian positions in 2014.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Spencer explicitly endorsed race-conscious admissions preferences for white applicants.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Spencer rejected equality as a social goal and prescribed distinct roles and rights for a guardian elite.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Spencer proposed a homeland specifically for people he classified as white and treated shared ancestry as the foundation of nationhood.

hereditarian-race.rationale: In the coauthored essay, Spencer attributed what the authors described as average racial differences in intelligence primarily to inheritance and natural selection.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Spencer considered a connected diaspora but said the ultimate goal was a territory that could gather white people from around the world.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Main describes Spencer’s rejection of rights belonging to people by birth and his account of rights as arising from membership in a collective.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Spencer proposed a single white ethnostate open to people of European descent from different countries.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Spencer treated language as one aspect of identity while making ancestry indispensable to membership in the nation he proposed.

military-force-beyond-defence.rationale: Spencer explicitly allowed for wars beyond self-defense when he believed they would expand his people or civilization.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Reflecting on the British Crown, Spencer argued that a monarch without governing authority projected a misleading image of continuity and probably should be abolished.

open-borders.rationale: Spencer called for a halt to mass immigration and proposed a future polity whose membership depended on ancestry.

political-violence-legitimate.rationale: In the civil case over Unite the Right, the jury found Spencer liable under Virginia law for civil conspiracy and for racial, religious, or ethnic harassment or violence.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Spencer explicitly supported EU membership for a Western-aligned Ukraine as part of a settlement that would end the fighting.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Spencer led a May 2017 demonstration opposing Charlottesville’s planned removal of its public monument to Confederate general Robert E. Lee.

race-based-immigration-restrictions.rationale: Spencer made European ancestry the criterion of entry to his proposed homeland and explicitly excluded groups he regarded as outside it.

race-social-construct.rationale: The coauthored essay explicitly treated racial categories as the product of biological evolution. Spencer separately described ancestry as fundamental to his own account of identity.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Spencer explicitly called for white identity politics and said he respected identitarians from other racial groups.

racial-pride.rationale: Spencer called for white people to cultivate racial consciousness and said he respected other groups expressing their own identities.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: The coauthored essay rejected structural racism as the primary explanation of racial gaps in schooling and economic attainment in the United States and attributed those gaps chiefly to alleged inherited differences.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Spencer called for a break from mass immigration and described legal immigration as particularly damaging because settlement is lasting.

religious-nation.rationale: Spencer envisioned the national community admitting both Christians and atheists on the basis of shared ancestry.

remove-other-ethnic-groups-from-country.rationale: Asked how people outside the designated group would be treated in his proposed state, Spencer endorsed ethnic population transfers modelled on postwar resettlement.

return-to-pre-conversion-religion.rationale: In Degeneration and Unity, Spencer and Brahmin explicitly opposed reviving old gods on grounds of ancestry alone and argued that a revival would have to serve a contemporary purpose.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Main documents Spencer’s rejection of inalienable human rights and his argument that rights arise from membership in a community.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Spencer described his intended order as revolutionary and explicitly rejected reproducing the U.S. Constitution and the existing system of mass elections.

state-harmful.rationale: Spencer wanted a state with a governing elite to defend the population and set the direction of society.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Spencer argued that Ukraine needed Western security guarantees and that remaining between blocs without them left it open to Russian domination.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Spencer proposed an empire with a large territory and said it might have to extend its control over much of the hemisphere.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Spencer included Medicare for All in his preferred political synthesis in 2020. In 2017 he had argued for a public insurance option.

notes: Research covered economic policy and work, elections and monarchy, race and citizenship, religion and culture, civil liberties, political methods, immigration, military alliances and Ukraine, conservation and climate, technology, and international economic policy. The 2026 book was checked through the preface and two author-published chapters. The Ukraine sources document a departure from his earlier pro-Russian commentary. The court source records civil liability and is used for conduct at Unite the Right.
